G L E U H R
Wellness Pvt Ltd
RECEPTIONIST
Role · KRAs · KPIs · SOP · Consequences
Reports to: Front Desk Manager  ·  Coordinates with: Counsellor, Doctor, Housekeeping
1  ·  Role Purpose
The Receptionist is the first and the last impression of the clinic. Every client is greeted, booked, attended and billed through the front desk, and the warmth, accuracy and discipline of that desk shape how the whole visit feels. The receptionist owns the front desk — greeting, appointments, calls, hospitality coordination, billing and records — to the standard the brand expects.
In one sentence.  Greet every client warmly, never lose an enquiry, keep the desk and the data clean, and make every payment transparent.

The desk sets the tone.  Reception is not a back-office function — it is the face of the branch. A client decides how they feel about the clinic in the first ten seconds at the desk and in the last ten seconds at billing. Hold both with the same care.
2  ·  Key Result Areas (KRAs)
Six KRAs. Each carries weight in monthly review.
KRA 1 — Greeting & Client Experience
Every client greeted within 10 seconds, by name, with a smile
Warm, professional tone on every interaction
Hospitality offered to every waiting client; client thanked on departure
Positive feedback / CSAT above target
KRA 2 — Appointment Management
Day's schedule reviewed before opening; dashboard kept open
Bookings accurate — no clashes, no double-booking
Confirmations sent a day ahead; appointments found by client name
Coordination with counsellor / doctor / therapist on flow
KRA 3 — Call & Message Handling
Calls answered promptly; 100% pick-up rate during duty hours
Missed-call / callback log maintained; all calls returned the same day
WhatsApp messages replied to within the duty-hour SLA
No enquiry lost — every lead logged and followed
KRA 4 — Billing Accuracy & Transparency
Amount and purpose stated before every collection
Bill / receipt generated and sent to the client's WhatsApp
Billing accuracy at 100% — no errors, no disputes
Zero off-system or cash-in-hand payments
KRA 5 — Records & CRM Hygiene
Client contact and WhatsApp details accurate and updated
Registration forms complete for every client
Leads tagged correctly; every enquiry logged
CRM data accuracy at 100%
KRA 6 — Front Desk Discipline & Brand Stewardship
Grooming and uniform to standard; desk tidy; no personal phone at the desk
Waiting area kept comfortable in coordination with housekeeping
Zero hard-line violations — off-system payments, data mishandling
Issues escalated to the FDM rather than argued with the client

4  ·  Standard Operating Procedure
Every working day follows this rhythm. The discipline is what makes the desk run.
Morning  ·  Before clients arrive
Review the full day's schedule before clinic hours; keep the booking dashboard open.
Ready the desk — forms, cards, stationery; switch on and check CRM, billing, phone, AC, lighting, music.
Confirm with housekeeping that reception, washrooms and water station are ready.
Join the reception huddle with the FDM.
The 10-second rule & find-by-name
Greet in ten seconds; never ask for a phone number first.  A client should be greeted, by name, within ten seconds of walking in — warmth before paperwork. And appointments are always located by the client's name, never by asking 'give me your number', which makes a client feel like a record rather than a guest.
Through the day
Greet every client within 10 seconds, by name; locate the appointment by name and check them in.
Offer water / tea / coffee; communicate any wait proactively.
Answer every call promptly; maintain the missed-call / callback log; send WhatsApp confirmations.
Bill transparently — state the amount and purpose, collect, send the WhatsApp receipt, record accurately.
Keep CRM and records accurate; log every enquiry and tag leads correctly.
Evening  ·  After clients leave
Confirm tomorrow's appointments and send confirmations.
Complete all callbacks in the log.
Reconcile and close billing with the FDM; hand over cash securely.
Update the CRM; tidy and lock the desk.
5  ·  Monthly Rhythm  ·  Front Desk Review
Monthly review with the Front Desk Manager on the scorecard, feedback and callbacks. Forward-looking on experience and discipline.
What it covers
Last month — scorecard average, feedback, callback completion; what worked, what didn't
This month's commitment — specific experience and accuracy targets
Top 3 issues to fix — with the support needed
Client-experience improvements — specific actions to lift feedback
Skill development — what to get sharper on (calls, billing, CRM)
Asks of the FDM — anything needed to hold the standard
Small things, held daily.  Reception excellence is not one big thing — it is a hundred small standards held every single day. The monthly review is where the pattern is seen and the next month's focus is set.
6  ·  Authority and Escalation
What Reception decides without escalation
Routine bookings, rescheduling and confirmations
Standard call and WhatsApp handling
Hospitality and waiting-area coordination
Standard billing within the published price list
What needs the FDM
Client complaint or a long-wait situation
Scheduling clash that cannot be resolved cleanly
Any billing query, discount or exception beyond standard
System / dashboard issue
Clinical — to the Doctor (via the FDM)
Any clinical question from a client — never advise clinically
Reaction or medical concern raised at the desk
What comes higher
Pressure to take an off-system payment or mishandle data — to the FDM / BM the same day
Anything that feels wrong at the desk
7  ·  Don'ts
Behaviours that are not acceptable, regardless of how busy the desk is.
Never take an off-system or cash-in-hand payment
Never lose, ignore or fail to log an enquiry
Never share client data improperly
Never argue with a client — acknowledge and escalate to the FDM
Never leave the desk unattended without cover
Never use a personal phone at the desk in front of clients
Never advise a client on a clinical matter
Never treat a standard as optional because the floor is busy
8  ·  Consequences Framework
Trigger
Response
Single-month miss on a KPI
Documented in 1-on-1 with the FDM; cause analysis; corrective plan agreed
Two consecutive months miss on the same KPI
Written notice; 30-day improvement plan with weekly check-ins
Three consecutive months miss
Formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with HR + FDM
Lost / unlogged enquiries, repeatedly
Written warning
Billing error or dispute, repeatedly
Written warning; billing re-training
Single off-system payment or data-mishandling violation
Same-day review; termination consideration
Serious dishonesty with the FDM
Single-incident termination consideration
9  ·  What 'Good' Looks Like — End of First Year
Clients greeted warmly within seconds, by name, every time.
No enquiry lost; callbacks cleared daily.
Billing accurate and transparent; receipts always sent.
CRM and records clean; forms complete.
The front desk feels calm, warm and in control even on a busy day.
